{{Short description|Theorem in group theory}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically in the field of [[group theory]], the '''McKay conjecture''' is a [[theorem]] of equality between two numbers: the number of irreducible [[complex number|complex]] [[character theory|characters]] of degree not divisible by a [[prime number]] <math>p</math> for a given finite group and the same number for the [[normalizer]] in that group of a [[Sylow theorems|Sylow <math>p</math>-subgroup]]. 

It is named after the Canadian mathematician [[John McKay (mathematician)|John McKay]], who originally stated a limited version of it as a [[conjecture]] in 1971, for the special case of <math>p=2</math> and [[simple group]]s. The conjecture was later generalized by other mathematicians to a more general conjecture for any prime value of <math>p</math> and more general groups.

In 2023, a [[mathematical proof|proof]] of the general conjecture was announced by [[Britta Späth]] and [[Marc Cabanes]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sloman |first=Leila |date=2025-02-19 |title=After 20 Years, Math Couple Solves Major Group Theory Problem |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/after-20-years-math-couple-solves-major-group-theory-problem-20250219/ |access-date=2025-02-20 |website=Quanta Magazine |language=en}}</ref>

== Statement ==

Suppose <math>p</math> is a prime number, <math>G</math> is a [[finite group]], and <math>P \leq G</math> is a Sylow <math>p</math>-subgroup. Define

:<math>\textrm{Irr}_{p'}(G) := \{\chi \in \textrm{Irr}(G) : p \nmid 
\chi(1) \}</math>

where <math>\textrm{Irr}(G)</math> denotes the set of complex [[Character theory#Definitions|irreducible characters]] of the group <math>G</math>. The McKay conjecture claims the equality

:<math>|\textrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)| = |\textrm{Irr}_{p'}(N_G(P))|</math>

where <math>N_G(P)</math> is the normalizer of <math>P</math> in <math>G</math>.

In other words, for any finite group <math>G</math>, the number of its [[irreducible representation|irreducible]] complex [[group representation|representations]] whose dimension is not divisible by <math>p</math> equals that number for the normalizer of any of its Sylow <math>p</math>-subgroups.  (Here we count [[isomorphic]] representations as the same.) 

== History ==
In McKay's original papers on the subject,<ref>{{cite journal |last=McKay |first=John |date=1971 |title=A new invariant for finite simple groups|volume=128 |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |pages=397}}</ref><ref>
{{cite journal |last=McKay |first=John |date=1972 |title=Irreducible representations of odd degree |doi=10.1016/0021-8693(72)90066-X |volume=20 |journal=[[Journal of Algebra]] |issue=2 |pages=416–418}}</ref> the statement was given for the prime <math>p=2</math> and simple groups, but examples of computations of <math>|\textrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)|</math> for odd primes or [[symmetric group]]s are mentioned. [[Martin Isaacs|Marty Isaacs]] also checked the conjecture for the prime 2 and [[solvable group]]s <math>G</math>.<ref>
{{cite journal |last=Isaacs |first=I. Martin |date=1973 |title=Characters of solvable and symplectic groups |doi=10.2307/2373731 |volume=95 |journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] |issue=3 |pages=594–635|jstor=2373731 }}</ref> The first appearance of the conjecture for arbitrary primes is in a paper by [[Jonathan Lazare Alperin |Jon L. Alperin]] giving also a version in [[Modular representation theory|block theory]], now called the '''Alperin–McKay conjecture'''.<ref>{{cite book
		| last1 = Alperin | first1 = Jon L.
		| year = 1976
		| title = Proceedings of the Conference on Finite Groups (Univ. Utah, Park City, Utah, 1975)
		| chapter = The main problem in block theory
		| publisher=Academic Press
		| pages=341–356
		| isbn = 978-3-540-20364-3
}}</ref>

== Proof ==

In 2007, [[Martin Isaacs]], [[Gunter Malle]] and [[Gabriel Navarro Ortega|Gabriel Navarro]] showed that the McKay conjecture reduces to the checking of a so-called '''inductive McKay condition''' for each [[finite simple group]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Isaacs |first1= I. M. |last2=Malle |first2=Gunter|last3=Navarro|first3=Gabriel |date=2007 |title=A reduction theorem for the McKay conjecture|doi=10.1007/s00222-007-0057-y |volume=170 |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |issue= 1 |pages=33–101 |bibcode= 2007InMat.170...33I }}
</ref><ref> {{cite book
 | last = Navarro | first = Gabriel
 | year = 2018
 | title = Character theory and the McKay conjecture
 | series = Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics
 | volume = 175
 | publisher = Cambridge University Press
 | isbn =978-1-108-42844-6
 }}</ref> This opens the door to a proof of the conjecture by using the [[classification of finite simple groups]].

The Isaacs−Malle−Navarro paper was also an inspiration for similar reductions for Alperin weight conjecture (named after [[Jonathan Lazare Alperin]]), its block version, the Alperin−McKay conjecture, and Dade's conjecture (named after [[Everett C. Dade]]).

The McKay conjecture for the prime 2 was proven by Britta Späth and [[Gunter Malle]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Malle |first1= Gunter |last2=Späth |first2=Britta|date=2016 |title=Characters of odd degree|doi=10.4007/annals.2016.184.3.6  |volume=184 |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |issue= 3 |pages=869–908|arxiv=1506.07690 }}</ref>

An important step in proving the inductive McKay condition for all simple groups is to determine the [[group action|action]] of the [[automorphism group]] <math>\textrm{Aut}(G)</math> on the set <math>\textrm{Irr}(G)</math> for each finite [[quasisimple group]] <math>G</math>. The solution was given by Späth<ref>{{cite journal
	| last = Späth
	| first = Britta
	| date = 2025
	| title = Extensions of characters in type D and the inductive McKay condition, II
	| arxiv =  2304.07373
| doi=10.1007/s00222-025-01354-9 |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]|volume=242|pages=45–122 }}</ref> in the form of an <math>\textrm{Aut}(G)</math>-equivariant [[Deligne–Lusztig theory#Jordan_decomposition|Jordan decomposition of characters]] for finite quasisimple groups of Lie type.

A proof of the McKay conjecture for all primes and all finite groups was announced by Britta Späth and Marc Cabanes in October 2023 in various conferences, a manuscript being available later in 2024.<ref>{{cite arXiv | eprint=2410.20392 | title=The McKay Conjecture on character degrees | author1=Marc Cabanes | author2=Britta Späth | class= RT |year=2024}}to appear Annals of Mathematics</ref>
